---
title: Add a data retention policy
description: Create a data retention policy to automatically drop historical data from your hypertables when it reaches a certain age
products: [cloud, self_hosted]

---

import * as C from "@constants";
import { Callout } from "@stainless-api/docs/components";
import { NumberedList, NumberedItem } from "@components/NumberedList";
import DoWithAi from "@components/DoWithAi.astro";

Retention policies drop entire {C.CHUNK}s once their time range falls outside your window, which is cheaper than deleting millions of rows one by one. {C.TIMESCALE_DB} schedules a background {C.JOB} to apply the policy for you.

<DoWithAi />

## Add a data retention policy

Add a data retention policy by using the
[`add_retention_policy`](/reference/timescaledb/data-retention/add_retention_policy) function.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Choose your ${C.HYPERTABLE} and retention interval`}>
Decide how long you want to keep data before dropping it. In this example, the {C.HYPERTABLE}
named `conditions` retains the data for 24 hours.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Call `add_retention_policy`">
```sql
SELECT add_retention_policy('conditions', INTERVAL '24 hours');
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

<Callout variant="note">
A data retention policy only allows you to drop {C.CHUNK}s based on how far they are
in the past. To drop {C.CHUNK}s based on how far they are in the future,
[manually drop {C.CHUNK}s](/learn/data-lifecycle/data-retention/manually-drop-chunks).
</Callout>

## Remove a data retention policy

Remove an existing data retention policy by using the
[`remove_retention_policy`](/reference/timescaledb/data-retention/remove_retention_policy) function. Pass it the name
of the {C.HYPERTABLE} to remove the policy from.

```sql
SELECT remove_retention_policy('conditions');
```

## See scheduled data retention {C.JOB}s

To see your scheduled data retention {C.JOB}s and their {C.JOB} statistics, query the
[`timescaledb_information.jobs`](/reference/timescaledb/informational-views/jobs) and
[`timescaledb_information.job_stats`](/reference/timescaledb/informational-views/job_stats) tables.
For example:

```sql
SELECT j.hypertable_name,
       j.job_id,
       config,
       schedule_interval,
       job_status,
       last_run_status,
       last_run_started_at,
       js.next_start,
       total_runs,
       total_successes,
       total_failures
  FROM timescaledb_information.jobs j
  JOIN timescaledb_information.job_stats js
    ON j.job_id = js.job_id
  WHERE j.proc_name = 'policy_retention';
```

The results look like this:

```sql
-[ RECORD 1 ]-------+-----------------------------------------------
hypertable_name     | conditions
job_id              | 1000
config              | {"drop_after": "5 years", "hypertable_id": 14}
schedule_interval   | 1 day
job_status          | Scheduled
last_run_status     | Success
last_run_started_at | 2022-05-19 16:15:11.200109+00
next_start          | 2022-05-20 16:15:11.243531+00
total_runs          | 1
total_successes     | 1
total_failures      | 0
```
